units.function: Database-backed route boundary tests for Agent visibility and task assignment after Paperclip's permission-model upgrade, including company-work visibility, cross-tenant non-disclosure and a target-scoped private-Agent assignment grant.
units.dependencyDirection: Agent-JWT identity enters issue/activity Express routes; routes consult Company scope, Agent JSON authorizationPolicy, Company membership and relational principalPermissionGrants; issue-related tables and activity are returned as Company work projections. Tests write policy/grant records directly to Postgres.
units.keyDataModels: Agent actor/company/run source; Agent authorizationPolicy with agentVisibility, assignmentPolicy and protectedAgent; Company membership; principal permission grant for tasks:assign_scope with assigneeAgentIds; issues/comments/documents/assets/attachments/work products/activity; HTTP 403/404 outcomes.
units.lifecycle: A private Agent is hidden from default directory discovery while its Company-owned work remains readable inside the tenant; cross-tenant reads stop at Company boundary with indistinguishable 404; same-Company open-target assignment succeeds by default; private-target assignment requires membership and a grant scoped to that exact Agent and remains denied for another target.
units.testAssessment: The three tests encode valuable privacy semantics and exact-scope behavior, but all were skipped because embedded Postgres support was unavailable, so no runtime pass is claimed. Missing cases include same-Company human visibility tiers, inactive/suspended/deleted principals, grant issuer authorization/provenance, self-grant and cross-Agent grant APIs, expiry/revocation, deny precedence, wildcard/escalation, role/budget/adapter/tool/data permission changes, approval, audit records, idempotency, concurrent revocation/assignment and stable error envelopes.
units.designRationale: Avoid turning private Agent-directory visibility into accidental secrecy of shared Company work, prevent cross-tenant existence leakage, and retain narrow explicit assignment access for protected targets after a permission-model expansion.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must distinguish principal discoverability from work/data confidentiality and support precise human-governed delegation without allowing Agents to manufacture authority or obscure the accountability chain.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the tenant-first 404 boundary, separate principal-directory/work/data policies and exact resource-scoped grants. Replace Agent JSON policy as authority with versioned Policy/Grant records tied to stable Principal and Organization IDs. Every grant must identify an authorized human grantor or approved policy decision, responsibility contract, purpose, scope, action/data capabilities, issue time, expiry, revocation and audit/evidence references. Apply explicit deny precedence and optimistic policy versions; evaluate assignment and data access transactionally; add self-escalation, confused-deputy, race and cross-deployment tests. Default Agent-to-Agent assignment should be an organizational policy, not an implicit universal right.
units.responsibilityConflict: The demonstrated private-target grant has no human grantor and no approval or responsibility contract, while same-company Agents can assign open targets by default. This permits work delegation without proving who is responsible, what permissions/data the assignee may use, or who authorized the relationship. Directory privacy also must not be mistaken for confidentiality of sensitive work artifacts.

units.securityFindings: POSITIVE: tenant scope is evaluated before more detailed policy and returns a non-oracular 404; private principal discovery does not silently hide Company-owned work; assignment grant scope is exact and does not spill to another private target. CRITICAL accountability gap for Company OS: the demonstrated grant has grantedByUserId null and no accountable-human approval or responsibility contract. HIGH default-delegation risk: a same-company Agent may assign any non-private Agent without an explicit capability grant. HIGH lifecycle gap: grant expiry, revocation, issuer authority, deny precedence and concurrent use are untested. HIGH data-policy ambiguity: comments, documents, attachments, activity and work products are all visible based on Company membership here, without per-data authorization/export contracts. MEDIUM contract gap: authorization failures use English error strings rather than stable structured codes. TEST GAP: the entire suite was skipped locally, so database/runtime behavior remains unverified in this audit environment.
